in_arabic.name: جہانگیر
in_arabic.long_meaning: جہانگیر هو اسم ملكي يُرمزُّ إلى الحكم المُطلق وَالطَاعة المُستَجدة، وَهو مُشتقّ من الجہاد وَالنَصر، وَهُوَ الَّذي يُمثِّلُ الصِدق وَالإِخلاص في الحكم، وَيَقُولُ الإِمامُ الشافعيُّ: "جہانگیر مِنَ الجَنودِ الَّذي يَغلبُ عَلَيهمُ، وَهُوَ الَّذي يَستَمِرُّ الحَربَ وَالسَلامَ"

in_urdu.name: جہانگیر
in_urdu.meaning: ملک جسے حکمرانی کا حق ہے اور اطاعت کی ضرورت ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: جہانگیر ایک ملكی نام ہے جو حکمرانی کے مطلق حق اور مطیعہ اطاعت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، یہ نام جہاد اور نصر سے ماخوذ ہے، اور یہ حکمران کا ایماندار اور اخلاقی ہونا ظاہر کرتا ہے، اور شافعي امام کی ایک روایت ہے: "جہانگیر جنگی فوج کی سربراہی کرتا ہے، اور وہ جنگ اور امن دونوں میں کامیاب ہوتا ہے"

in_hindi.name: जहाँगीर
in_hindi.meaning: जिसे शासन का अधिकार है और समर्पण की आवश्यकता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: जहाँगीर एक राजा का नाम है जो शासन के पूर्ण अधिकार और समर्पण की आवश्यकता को दर्शाता है, यह नाम जिहाद और नصر से मिलकर बना है, और यह एक शासक के ईमानदार और नैतिक होने को दर्शाता है, और शाफई का एक कथन है: "जहाँगीर युद्ध की फौज का कमांडर होता है, और वह दोनों युद्ध और शांति में सफल होता है"

in_pashto.name: جهانگیر
in_pashto.meaning: ملک جهانگیر د هکمني حق لري او اطاعتو په ضرورت لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: جهانگیر د مليکي نوم دی، چې د هکمني مطلق حق او مطيعې اطاعتو په ښودي، د جهاد او نصر څخه اخستل شوی دی، او د جهانگیر د یو حاکم په ښودي کی چې په دې ډول د هکمني په توګه وده کوي او د جهاد په لور تګ کوي، په دې ډول د دوی د ناڅاپيرو ځواکو د پوځي مشر په توګه کار کوي، په دې ډول د جهاد او صلح په ډول له پوهېدو سره د دې ته ښودي چې دوی د سولې او صلح په لور هم د نړۍ د پوځي مشرانو په څېر وده کوي.

in_english.name: Jahangeer
in_english.meaning: a ruler with absolute power and the need for submission
in_english.long_meaning: Jahangeer is a name that signifies absolute rule and the need for submission. It is derived from the Arabic roots of jihad and nasr, and it represents the truth and sincerity of a ruler. According to Imam Shafi'i, Jahangeer is a name that refers to a warrior who is victorious in war and peace, and who leads his troops to victory in both battles. In Islamic tradition, Jahangeer is a name that symbolizes courage, strength, and leadership, and it is often associated with the qualities of a just and fair ruler.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jahangeer carries a powerful cultural impact, as it symbolizes strength, accomplishment, and triumph. In Islamic history, there have been numerous figures with this name who exhibited extraordinary courage, determination, and victory over adversity. For example, Jahangeer Khan was a Mughal emperor (1562-1627 CE) who expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest territorial extent and successfully fought against the threat from the Persian and Afghan invasions. Named after him, the name inspires a sense of fearlessness and conquest in the contemporary world.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Jahangeer is rooted in the idea of overcoming challenges and achieving mastery. According to Islamic teachings, every individual is granted the ability to overcome the trials of life through faith, patience, and perseverance. The name symbolizes the inner strength, courage, and determination that each person requires to face the hardships of life and emerge victorious. It reminds us that success in this world and the hereafter is not given; it is earned through hard work, self-improvement, and steadfastness in the face of adversity. Therefore, the name Jahangeer serves as a powerful motivator for the believer to strive for excellence, to persevere in the face of challenges, and to remain steadfast in their faith and pursuit of wisdom and virtue.

historical_references.reference: Jahangeer was the name of the Mughal emperor, Jahangir, who ruled from 1605 to 1627. He succeeded his father, Akbar, and expanded the Mughal empire through military campaigns, particularly in the Deccan region of India. Jahangir is also known for his patronage of arts and architecture, notably the Taj Mahal, which he built as a mausoleum for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

Jahangir was the fourth Mughal emperor, born on August 25, 1562, in Lahore, India. He was the son of Akbar and his favorite wife, Mariam-uz-Zamani. Jahangir was known for his love of hunting, which was a major part of his life, and his patronage of art and architecture, which led to the construction of many famous buildings, including the Red Fort in Delhi and the Taj Mahal in Agra.
